newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel court orders jail for police who beat Arabs.
newsitem.headline: Israel court orders jail for police who beat Arabs.

text.p: An Israeli court on Thursday sentenced two paramilitary border policemen filmed brutalising Palestinians to eight months in jail, Israel radio said.
"The two policemen degraded the border police uniform and must receive a punishment that will deter others," the radio quoted the judge as saying.
The court ordered border policemen Tsahi Shamaya, 19, and David Ben Abu, 20, to serve eight months in prison and a further 12 months of suspended jail time.

The verdict was issued a day after the Israeli rights group B'Tselem released a 31-page report detailing what it said were 15 cases of "beatings, degradation and serious abuse" of Palestinians by security forces over the last three months.
Shamaya and Ben Abu were filmed by an amateur cameraman last October brutalising six Palestinians caught in Jerusalem without entry permits.
The videotape, showing the two policemen kicking some of the Palestinians in the head, kneeing another in the stomach and forcing others to do push-ups, was broadcast across the world.
The tape, which lasted more than half an hour, showed the policemen slapping Palestinians after forcing them to lie flat on the ground and riding one like a donkey.
The men were charged with aggravated assault and abuse of authority.
Witnesses said family members erupted from their seats in rage after hearing the verdict. One woman was evicted for calling the judge a "leftist".

"Beating and ill-treatment of Palestinians, especially at roadblocks and especially by the border police, is a very widespread and very serious phenomenon," B'Tselem activist Yuval Ginbar told Reuters.
"We're talking about at least dozens of people held at roadblocks every day, many having tried to pass without licence, and many of these are almost routinely beaten or humiliated," he said.

Israel's Channel One television on Wednesday broadcast what it said was another case of border police brutality involving two Palestinian labourers. It said the two were so badly beaten on Tuesday that they required hospital treatment.
It interviewed Palestinian cousins Ahmed Moussa, 19, and Mahmoud Ghneim, 27, who lay side by side in a hospital in the West Bank town of Beit Jala.

The television said they were beaten after entering Israel without permits in the face of a closure imposed on the West Bank following a July 30 suicide attack in Israel. It said three border policemen beat the two in an isolated wood.

"Each one of them carried a club and administered beatings. One of them asked if my chest was all right and hit me in the chest. There were three who hit me," said Moussa, breathing heavily through a hospital mask.
"One of them pointed an M-16 rifle at my head -- he pointed the rifle next to my ear and told me: 'Now you'll get out of here. If I see you again, I will kill you. You must die'," Moussa said.
Showing his bloodied right side to the camera, Ghneim said the border policemen had tied his leg to a jeep and dragged him along the ground for 150 to 200 metres (yards).

The television said Ghneim managed to make his way to a main street where Israelis picked him up in their car and took him to hospital for treatment. Israel's Justice Ministry was investigating the incident.
